title: refactor(types,collaboration,data-objectstack,plugin-designer,providers): one authority each for ConnectionState, VersionEntry and ThemeProviderProps (objectui#6349, batch 10)
body:
Refs #6349 (batch 10)

Clause-②: yes

Batch 10 of the one-authority burn-down, on the claim `6093179763`. It covers three `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` rows from the collaboration and providers packages, none with an `@object-ui/types` side. Two rows converge here. The third, `ConnectionState`, stopped with measured options in round 1 and converges in round 2 (above), because the rules this card has applied do not settle it (see "The stop" below).

*(Round 1.)* Implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8` (the seat's session; this was a subagent dispatch).

## Round 2 (head `65da7a995`): all three rows converge

Brought up to round 2 by the seat (`domain:ui` seat 3). The round-1 text below is kept and marked where round 2 supersedes it.

- **`ConnectionState`:** ruled **A** by the seat's claim amendment `6093405166` on objectui#6349, under batch 3's rule and batch 4's `UndoableOperation` precedent, with the maintainer's veto window open.
  - The one declaration now lives in `@object-ui/types` (`data.ts`, beside `DataSource`) and is published from the types barrel.
  - collaboration's `useRealtimeSubscription.ts` and data-objectstack's `index.ts` are plain re-exports of it.
- **`KNOWN_COLLISIONS`:** 10 → **7** rows.
- **Published surface:** types 708 → 709 (`ConnectionState` joins). collaboration 39 = 39 and data-objectstack 104 = 104, with each copy type-equal to the types declaration. plugin-designer, providers and react are unchanged by round 2.
- **Emitted output:** no `.js` file differs.
- **Changesets added in round 2:** `@object-ui/types` **`minor`** (a new name), and `@object-ui/collaboration` and `@object-ui/data-objectstack` `patch`. ⛔ No `major`.
- **Round-2 gates at `65da7a995`:**
  - the gate: 11 of 11 pass;
  - types, collaboration and data-objectstack with the gate: 457 files and 11,307 tests passed;
  - the types, collaboration, data-objectstack and app-shell type-checks and `type-check:scripts` exit 0;
  - `check:doc-snippets`: 785 of 785 blocks judged, 0 failed. `check:readme-exports` is OK;
  - ablation S3 (stale) and F3a/F3b (fresh) went red as predicted, with restores proven blob-equal.

## What converged: `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` goes from 10 to 8 rows (round 1; 7 after round 2)

### `VersionEntry`: two meanings. The designer's side becomes `VersionHistoryEntry`

- **Member diff.** Both have `version`, `timestamp`, `userId` and `userName`; `userName` is optional in collaboration and required in the designer. Only collaboration's has `id`, `changes` (a per-field before/after diff that `revertToVersion` and `compareVersions` replay) and `message`. Only the designer's has `description` and `isCurrent`. Collaboration's is a version its `useConflictResolution` hook records. The designer's is a row its `VersionHistory` timeline displays.
- **Dependency edge:** neither package depends on the other. collaboration depends on `i18n` and `types`, and plugin-designer's dependency list has no collaboration.
- **Reach, read on the built entries:** the collaboration root publishes `VersionEntry`. The plugin-designer root does not. Its entry exports the `VersionHistory` component, but neither `VersionEntry` nor `VersionHistoryProps`, and the `components/index.ts` barrel that re-exported it has no importer. So the rename removes no published name: the plugin-designer root has 38 names before and 38 after. Batch 6's `DesignerConfirmDialogState` row had the same shape.
- **Readers:** none in the repo outside each package's own files, and 0 hits in `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 (control: `RealtimeConfig` and `ThemeMode` hit there).

### `ThemeProviderProps`: two providers. providers' side becomes `ThemePreferenceProviderProps`

- **Member diff.** providers' has `defaultTheme?: ThemePreference`, `storageKey?` and `children`. react's has `themes?`, `defaultTheme?: string`, `defaultMode?: ThemeMode`, `persist?`, `storageKey?`, `target?` and `children`. The shared key `defaultTheme` means two things: a MODE on providers' side (`'dark'`) and a theme NAME on react's (`'my-theme'`). Neither provider wraps the other. providers' provider stores one mode and toggles the `light` / `dark` class. react's registers `Theme` documents and writes CSS variables.
- **Dependency edge:** neither package depends on the other. providers depends only on `types`; react depends on `core`, `data-objectstack`, `i18n`, `types` and the spec.
- **Reach:** both roots published the name, measured on the built entries. The providers root now publishes `ThemePreferenceProviderProps` instead, with identical members (23 names before and 23 after). The react root is unchanged (300 = 300). react's theme system is the general one: `@object-ui/types`' theme module names react's `ThemeProvider` as the one that applies a `Theme`. So react keeps the general name.
- **Readers:** none in the repo through either entry. The README, docs and examples teach the components, never the props type. 0 hits in `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0. This is therefore the zero-reader rename of a published name that the card's rules already settle (batch 7's `GroupAggregationConfig`, batch 8's `ListViewSwitcherProps`), and it is not a stop.
- **What an old import does now,** measured against the rebuilt entry: it fails with **TS2724**. That error's "Did you mean" names the `ThemeProvider` component, not the replacement. Following the suggestion fails too (**TS2749**, a value used as a type). Nothing compiles silently wrong, and the changeset says this.
- **Value names:** the two `ThemeProvider` components (and `useTheme`) keep their names. They are outside the gate's type-level bound, in the same way batch 9 kept the two `AppShell` components.

## The stop: `ConnectionState` (round 1; ruled A in `6093405166` and implemented in round 2)

- **Measured.** The two declarations are the SAME five-member union in a different source order. The two built entries' `ConnectionState` are type-equal: a mutual-equality probe exits 0, the same assertion flipped exits 2 (TS2322), and a control that drops one member is not equal.
- **Dependency edge:** neither depends on the other. collaboration has `i18n` and `types`; data-objectstack has `core`, `types`, `client` and the spec. Both already depend on `@object-ui/types`.
- **Readers through the entries:** data-objectstack's has 5 reader files, app-shell's `AppContent`, `AppHeader`, `ConnectionStatus` and `ConsoleLayout`, and the console's `dataSource.ts` re-export. collaboration's has 0 named readers, but it is the published state type of `useRealtimeSubscription`, which app-shell's `ObjectView` mounts. 0 hits in `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0.
- **So:** same thing ⇒ re-point. The re-point is dependency-illegal, and batch 3's rule forbids adding a dependency, so the rules do not settle the row.

| option | what | files beyond the claim | grades |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A (recommended)** | Move the one declaration down into `@object-ui/types`, which both packages already depend on. collaboration and data-objectstack each re-export it. | a `types` source file (beside `DataSource` in `data.ts` is natural) and the `types` barrel | `types` minor (one new name); collaboration and data-objectstack patch (shape and name sets unchanged) |
| B | Rename collaboration's to `RealtimeConnectionState`, published at its root in place of the old name (0 readers) | none | collaboration minor, breaking note |
| C | Retire collaboration's exported name (0 readers) and keep a module-local type | none | collaboration minor, breaking note |
| D (refused) | Re-point one package at the other | needs a new dependency | n/a: batch 3's rule, and a realtime hook would pull in the ObjectStack adapter and client |

Why A, along the four axes:
- **Real business need:** both sides are live and measured identical. A is the only option that keeps them identical by construction.
- **Long-term fitness:** A gives one authority. B and C name one vocabulary twice, so the gate stops seeing the pair while the two copies stay free to drift. That trades a visible collision for an invisible one. Precedents for moving a declaration down: batch 4's `UndoableOperation`, objectui#8261's `TranslateFn` and objectui#7664's Kanban trio.
- **Keeping AI from writing it wrong:** with A, one name has one meaning and an auto-import cannot pick the wrong copy. With B, an author must know that two identically shaped names exist.
- **Startup scope:** A adds one name to `types` and removes a duplicate. No capability is added.

## Changeset grades

- `@object-ui/providers` **minor** with a breaking note: a name leaves the root, and the note names the migration and the measured TS2724 / TS2749.
- `@object-ui/plugin-designer` **minor** with a nothing-breaks note: only the type name in the published declaration of `VersionHistory`'s `versions` prop changes. This is the same grading batch 6 gave `useConfirmDialog`'s `DesignerConfirmDialogState`.
- Round 2 adds `@object-ui/types` `minor` (`ConnectionState` joins), and `@object-ui/collaboration` and `@object-ui/data-objectstack` `patch` (each site becomes a re-export).

## Verification (head `48285b125`, base `1b2d0160`)

- **Built entries:** one TypeScript program over all five entries per tree, with dist rebuilt for the two touched packages. The name sets are collaboration 39 = 39, data-objectstack 104 = 104, plugin-designer 38 = 38, providers 23 = 23 (`ThemeProviderProps` leaves, `ThemePreferenceProviderProps` joins) and react 300 = 300.
- **Emitted JS is byte-identical** in providers and plugin-designer. Only `.d.ts` / `.d.ts.map` files differ, so no first-load byte moves.
- **The gate** (`one-authority-per-exported-name-6273`) passes 11 of 11.
- **Suites:** the providers suite, the `VersionHistory` locale test and the gate ran at the final head: 5 files and 26 tests passed. The plugin-designer package suite ran at `ef2e5845b`, whose code is identical to the head (the later commit changes one changeset only): 46 files and 449 tests passed.
- **Type-checks** (each script name echoed): providers, plugin-designer, react, collaboration, data-objectstack, fields (a providers dependant), app-shell (a dependant of both) and `type-check:scripts` all exit 0. app-shell's first attempt exited 2 with TS2307 on unbuilt dependencies. That was an unmet prerequisite, not a measurement, and it exited 0 once its dependency closure was built.
- **Checks:** `check:control-bytes` OK, `check:test-path-roots` OK, `check:changeset-claims` OK, `check:pending-changeset-literals` OK, `check:readme-exports` OK (582 of 582 self-imports judged, after building the 7 packages its first run reported unbuilt), `check:doc-snippets` (785 of 785 blocks judged, 0 failed), `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), changeset presence OK and no-major OK. eslint on the touched files reports 0 errors and 3 warnings, all on lines this diff does not touch.
- **Ablation** through `ablation-replace`, with predictions written first. Control: 11 passed. All four legs went red as predicted, each with 1 failed and 10 passed in "declares no name twice outside the named, shrinking baseline":
  - S1 (`VersionEntry` row restored): stale, both files listed;
  - F1 (the designer spelling `VersionEntry` again): fresh, "a NEW colliding name";
  - S2 (`ThemeProviderProps` row restored): stale, both files;
  - F2 (providers spelling `ThemeProviderProps` again): fresh.
  - Every leg was restored blob-equal to HEAD, and the tree is clean afterwards.
  - The first S1 and S2 attempts were no-ops: my replacement re-contained the anchor, so the tool refused before running the gate. They were re-run with a replacement that does not.
- **Governed-queue guard:** NOT GOVERNED over the 8 paths.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- Three components share the value name `ThemeProvider`: providers', react's and app-shell's chrome one, which the app-shell root exports. This is outside the gate's type-level bound, like the `AppShell` pair.
- plugin-designer's `CollaborationProvider` spells a fourth, unnamed connection-state union inline: four members, no `reconnecting`. It is not a collision under the gate. If option A lands, it has a name to point at.
- plugin-designer's `components/index.ts` barrel has no importer, like the `hooks/index.ts` barrel batch 6 noted.
- Batch 8's comment riders wait for a batch that touches their files. None of them is in this batch.
